name: Ratio Meaning, Units, and Simplification
description: Read a ratio as a comparison, convert quantities to the same unit, simplify it, compare ratios, and connect part-to-part with part-to-whole.
script_scope: Teach ratio as a comparison of two quantities in the same units and as the fraction a/b. Cover antecedent and consequent, converting units before comparing, simplifying by a common factor, building equivalent ratios, ratios containing decimals or fractions, comparing two ratios by cross-products, converting part-to-part ratios into part-to-whole fractions or percentages, and checking whether a proposed total can fit a whole-number ratio. Use concrete counts, money, time and length. Learners should know exactly what each term represents before calculating.

name: Proportion and Missing Terms
description: Recognize equal ratios, use the product of means and extremes, and find missing, third, fourth, and mean proportionals.
script_scope: Teach proportion as equality of two ratios and derive the cross-product rule: in a:b = c:d, ad = bc. Use it to find a missing term in integer, decimal and fractional proportions. Cover fourth proportional, third proportional, mean proportional sqrt(ab), continued proportion, and simple proportion equations with an expression such as (x+1):8 = 3:4. Emphasize preserving term order and checking by comparing the two final ratios.

name: Linking and Chaining Ratios
description: Join pairwise ratios into one common ratio across three or four quantities without losing the shared middle term.
script_scope: Teach how to combine A:B and B:C by making the shared term B equal, then extend to four quantities. Include pairwise ratios given as fractions, equations such as 2A=3B=4C, inverse-looking equalities, and chained relations across shares, ages or incomes. Show both the scale-to-common-middle method and the multiply-ratios shortcut for endpoints. End with using a chained ratio plus a total to recover actual values.

name: Algebra with Ratios and Expressions
description: Turn a known ratio into convenient multiples and evaluate or reverse-engineer algebraic expressions involving the same quantities.
script_scope: Teach the substitution habit x:y = m:n -> x=mk, y=nk. Use it to evaluate ratios of linear expressions, squares and cubes; simplify expressions by dividing through by y or y^2; and solve backwards when a ratio such as (2x+3y):(3x+5y) is given. Include reciprocal-expression patterns and a quadratic relation that can produce two possible ratios. Learners should avoid solving for x and y separately when only x:y is needed.

name: Compound, Duplicate, and Transformed Ratios
description: Use compounded, reciprocal, duplicate, sub-duplicate, triplicate, and componendo-dividendo transformations confidently.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's named ratio transformations: compounded ratio, reciprocal ratio, duplicate and sub-duplicate ratios, triplicate and sub-triplicate ratios, and componendo and dividendo. Build each from a numerical ratio before using symbols. Include geometric-chain relations x:y=y:z=z:u and identity-style questions where a transformed ratio is easier than solving individual values. Make clear that squaring or cubing applies to both terms.

name: Dividing a Total in a Ratio
description: Convert ratio parts into actual shares, including inverse-share conditions, fractional relations, and group distributions.
script_scope: Teach ratio shares as equal-sized units: add the ratio terms, find one unit, then multiply. Cover two-, three- and four-way division; inverse shares from equal multiples such as 3A=4B=7C; fraction relations such as A=3/2 B and B=7/4 C; conditions involving a share versus the combined shares of others; minimum whole-number distributions from fractional ratios; and group problems where different numbers of men, women and children receive different per-person shares. Include a nested split capstone.

name: Ratio Puzzles with Sums, Differences, and Products
description: Use a ratio together with a sum, difference, product, average, square relation, or LCM to recover the actual numbers.
script_scope: Teach the common multiplier model: numbers in ratio m:n are mk and nk. Determine k from a known sum, difference, product, average, difference of squares, sum of squares, or LCM when the ratio terms are coprime. Extend to three-number patterns and simple cost/count stories. Learners should choose the shortest condition, solve for k, and then answer only the requested quantity.

name: Changing Ratios after Adding, Removing, or Transferring
description: Model how a ratio changes when the same amount or a one-sided amount is added, removed, or transferred.
script_scope: Teach changing-ratio equations. Start with adding or subtracting the same number from both terms, then add/remove people from one group, transfer units from one group to another, and handle age ratios after a fixed number of years. Include mixture questions where only water or milk is added, and two-condition problems that determine both original quantities. Emphasize that ratio terms are not actual values until multiplied by a common scale.

name: Income, Expenditure, and Savings Ratios
description: Connect income, spending, savings, salary changes, and allowances when each relationship is given as a ratio or percentage.
script_scope: Teach Income = Expenditure + Savings inside ratio problems. Cover income and expenditure ratios with equal savings, finding savings ratios, salaries linked by a given ratio plus a percentage contribution or allowance, two-year income and expense ratios, and three-person cases where saved percentages convert income ratios into savings ratios. Use common multipliers instead of guessing actual salaries until one absolute amount fixes the scale.

name: Direct Variation
description: Translate 'varies directly as' into a constant-multiplier equation, including powers, roots, and shifted quantities.
script_scope: Teach direct variation x ∝ y -> x=ky and how to determine k from one known pair. Extend to y ∝ x^2, y ∝ x^3, y ∝ sqrt(x), and y ∝ (x+c). Include physical-style applications from the chapter such as pendulum time versus square root of length and value of a diamond versus a power of weight/volume. Show how ratios often eliminate k entirely when comparing two cases.

name: Inverse and Combined Variation
description: Use constant products for inverse variation and combine direct and inverse factors, including inverse-square relationships.
script_scope: Teach inverse variation x ∝ 1/y -> xy=k and test possible pairs using the constant product. Cover equal-distance speed/time, gear revolutions versus number of cogs, inverse-square intensity, and combined forms such as resistance directly proportional to length and inversely proportional to radius squared. Include a relation made from one direct and one inverse term, y=ax+b/x, using two observations to determine constants.

name: Mixture and Composition Ratios
description: Track component fractions when mixtures are combined, strengthened, diluted, or repeatedly replaced.
script_scope: Teach component ratio -> component fraction first. Cover equal-volume mixtures, unequal quantities, target mixtures solved by alligation-style reasoning, adding a pure component, adding water, evaporation where solute stays fixed, mixing alloys or teas with different compositions/prices, and the repeated replacement rule x(1-y/x)^n. Keep the invariant component visible and end with a repeated milk-water replacement capstone.

name: Weighted Ratio Applications
description: Combine a count ratio with a rate, fare, wage, price, or percentage to find weighted totals and overall change.
script_scope: Teach that a ratio of people or units and a ratio/rate per person combine through multiplication. Cover weighted average charges when attendance differs, fare-class income, group wages, employee-count and wage changes, category expenditure with different price increases, weighted profit across product types, proportional marks with equal maximum marks, and linked old/new income ratios. Learners should compute contribution = count × rate before combining.

name: Data Sufficiency with Ratios
description: Decide whether one statement, either statement, both statements, or neither gives enough information to determine a ratio or actual value.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's five data-sufficiency outcomes. Distinguish a ratio that fixes only shape from information that fixes scale. Test Statement I alone, Statement II alone, then both only when needed. Include ratio-only questions, actual salary/count questions, age ratios across time, redundant restatements, and cases where even two ratios leave the common multiplier unknown. The learner must decide sufficiency without doing unnecessary full calculations.
